description: Mechanics-15 on hex, 2D smoke: GPT-6 Astra alone on the five hex mazes of run_config.mechanics_15_hex_2d.json, with the same cell and settings, to see whether the tiling alone costs a model that is near BFS-optimal on the square mazes.
_note_no_conditions: No conditions key => single (default) cell built from experiment_config overlay. Do NOT add conditions (that would re-enable the sweep).
_note_render: render.backend=multigrid: the MultiGrid backend, which steps square and hex tasks through the same R1 rulebook as MiniGrid (gridworld.world_model) and draws frames in the MiniGrid look (gridworld.render2d: same palette and icons, pointy-top hex cells of ~1039 px each against MiniGrid's 1024, 18x18 frames 641x550 against 576x576). The run label is multigrid_r<RENDER2D_VERSION>. Everything else is the 2D run's: the minimal prompt and its action list are unchanged, TURN_LEFT/TURN_RIGHT turn 60 degrees and MOVE_FORWARD enters the neighbouring hex. The minigrid and 3D backends refuse hex mazes and the cardinal action space is refused on hex (check_tasks_runnable, before Stage 2).
_note_launch: Launch with difficulty_max_static_score = 20000 (--difficulty-max-static-score 20000): the largest static score of the five is the hex M10's, about 19,230 (rotating ~14,810, the others ~2,830-3,610). Hex scores run 2.3-2.5x their square originals because search_space_size (BFS states explored) grows with six facings and six-phase turntables, so composite run scores are not comparable to R2's (normalized by 8000): compare success, steps and optimality ratio. Stage 2 takes about 30 s for all five. Measured BFS (hex / square): portals 100 / 90, death 130 / 121, rotating 134 / 128, frozen 140 / 131, M10 83 / 75.
_note_model_params: GPT-6 Astra exactly as in run_config.mechanics_15_2d.json (reasoning_effort=xhigh, flex, image_detail=high, prompt cache on) except spend_cap_usd=100, which sits above the projection below if every episode runs to its 3x step cap (~$82) and stops the worker early if caching fails.
_note_cost: Projected with the 2D note's Astra measurements (s ~399 tokens per history step, t ~500 tail, ~220 output per query, flex prices $5 / $0.50 cache read / $6.25 1h write / $25 output per 1M) on these mazes' hex BFS lengths (100, 130, 134, 140, 83; 587 in all, against 1,532 for the 15 square mazes). A hex frame has about the same pixel count as a square one (641x550 vs 576x576), so s is assumed unchanged. If every episode runs 1x / 2x / 3x (the step cap) its shortest path: ~$13 / ~$41 / ~$82. An episode ends earlier on death or after progress_stall_k=30 steps without a new state.
